title: How many groups of five are on the Lebombo bone?
description: The twenty nine notches of the Lebombo bone are counted off five at a time, giving full groups and a few left over. Keeko's doubt is that the last few notches make a sixth group too.
teaching_notes: One idea: grouping tally marks in fives makes a long row easy to read, and what cannot fill a group stays as a leftover. Watch for students who count the short last bunch as a full group.

source: The Lebombo bone has 29 notches. Group them in fives. How ma
video_script.why: The child sees that tally marks are easier to read in groups of five, and that notches which cannot fill a group are the leftover.
video_script.substitution: Draw the notches in a row and count them off five at a time, then see what is left.
video_script.anchor: the Lebombo bone, a bone from South Africa about forty four thousand years old, with a row of twenty nine notches cut along it
video_script.wrong_answer: six groups, because the last few notches make a group too
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko counts the last few notches as a sixth group. A group needs five notches, and only four are left, so they are a leftover.
video_script.payoff_line: Five full groups of five, and four notches left over

final_answer.spoken: five groups of five and four more

never_show: the answer card before the last beat of the board solution
maths_rules: tally marks: one mark cut for each object counted
counting off five at a time: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, so there are 5 full groups
video_script.design: One idea: group the marks in fives and keep the leftover apart. The bone and its row of notches stay on the stage; a loop closes round each full group.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the Lebombo bone.
<bookmark mark='bone'/>It was found in South Africa, and it is about forty four thousand years old. It has twenty nine notches.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Group the notches in fives. How many full groups are there, and how many notches are left over?

beats.on_screen: the bone holds still and the question mark glows

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board and the question mark glows

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the notches move to the stage; each notch is joined to one object; the label tally marks appears; a small box of 3 marks is read at a glance, and a box of 7 marks is not

marks.tally: each notch is joined to one object and the label tally marks appears
marks.glance: a small box of marks is read at a glance, and a box of many marks is hard to read

narration: <bookmark mark='tally'/>Marks cut into a surface, one for each object counted, are called tally marks.
<bookmark mark='glance'/>Most people cannot see a group of five or more marks at a glance. Grouping the marks in fives helps.

beats.on_screen: Given: 29 notches on the bone; group them in fives

marks.given: the facts are written as the given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, twenty nine notches on the bone, to be grouped in fives.

beats.on_screen: To find: the number of full groups, and the notches left over

marks.find: the words To find are written under the given

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the full groups, and the notches left over.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: count off 5 notches at a time: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25; a loop closes round each group, 5 loops in all

marks.m1: loops close round the notches five at a time, and the running count 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 appears under the loops

narration: <bookmark mark='s1'/>Step one, count off five notches at a time.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Five, ten, fifteen, twenty, twenty five. That makes five full groups.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: notches in the full groups = 5 groups × 5 notches = 5 × 5 = 25

marks.m2: the five loops glow, each marked with five notches, and 5 × 5 = 25 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='s2'/>Step two, count the notches inside the full groups.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Five groups of five notches is five times five, which is twenty five.

marks.m3: 29 − 25 = 4 is written, and the last notches outside the loops glow

narration: <bookmark mark='s3'/>Step three, take the notches in full groups from all the notches.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Twenty nine minus twenty five is four, so four notches are left over.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: check: 5 × 5 + 4 = 25 + 4 = 29, which is all the notches

marks.m4: the loops and the leftover notches slide together and total 29

narration: <bookmark mark='s4'/>Step four, put the groups back to check.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Twenty five and four make twenty nine, which is all the notches on the bone.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 5 groups of five and 4 more

marks.res: the five loops and the four leftover notches glow

narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>Five full groups of five, and four notches left over.
<bookmark mark='res'/>The twenty nine notches read as five groups of five and four more.

beats.on_screen: Keeko appears beside the board with a raised hand
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows six groups; the last bunch at the end of the row is looped and holds only 4 notches with one empty gap; the bubble is struck through

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble shows six groups and loops the last bunch
marks.short: the last bunch holds four notches with an empty gap where a fifth notch should be
marks.fix: the bubble is struck through and the last bunch is marked as the leftover

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks there are six groups, because the last few notches make a group too.
<bookmark mark='short'/>Look at that last bunch. It has an empty gap where a fifth notch should be.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>A group needs five notches, so that bunch is not a full group.
